title: The Origin and Development of Applause

passage.title: The Origin and Development of Applause
paragraphs: A. Scholars are not completely sure where applause first began, but the most common form—clapping hands together—became standard in Western culture during and after performances. In the time of the Roman Republic (509 BC – 27 BC), plays often ended with the lead actor shouting "Valete et plaudite!" which means "Goodbye and applaud!" This was the signal for the audience to show approval by clapping hands and making loud noise. Because of this, applause soon became a way to control crowds. In Rome, a group of professionals called laudiceni appeared. These were "people who clapped for their dinner"—they were paid to join the audience and influence how others reacted. Actors would hire about a dozen of them to spread out in the crowd, make the applause last longer, or even start "spontaneous" cheers and shouts of praise if they wanted to be extra bold.

B. The Roman Republic came to an end and was replaced by the Roman Empire (27 BC – 476 AD) where applause became a way for leaders to interact directly with their citizens. One of the chief methods they used to estimate their standing with the people was gauging the greetings they got when they entered the arena.

C. Clever leaders of the ancient world researched their rivals, too. Cicero, the Roman lawyer, would send friends to stand around outside the arena, taking notes to see what kind of greeting each official got when he entered, the better to see who was beloved by the people, and who was not.

D. Around the first centuries AD, those systems of applause became more and more elaborate. Applause no longer meant, simply, 'claps'. While Greco-Roman audiences certainly smacked their palms together the same way we do today, their overall strategies of applause were much more varied than clapping alone.

E. Although the way people applaud may have changed over time, the desire to control it stayed the same. In the 16th century, French poet Daurat is said to have revived the old Roman habit of hiring people to clap. In France, these hired clappers were called a "claque." Daurat gave free tickets to his shows to those who agreed to applaud afterward.
By the early 1820s, claques became organized, with a Paris agency that offered clappers' services.
Historian William B. Cohen explains the detailed price lists these agencies gave to customers: polite clapping cost a certain amount of francs, and excited applause cost more. The claque was divided into types: the rieurs (laughers) laughed hard at jokes; the pleureurs (criers) pretended to cry during shows; the commissaires (officers) memorized a play or music and pointed out its good parts. This custom spread to Milan, Vienna, and London before it went out of style. The claque lost its influence when people learned about its secrets.

F. And clapping itself changed over time. In the 18th century, symphonies and concerts became more serious, like religious events full of respect and quiet focus. Audiences learned that knowing when to maintain silence—and when to clap—was a sign of good taste and manners. Applause turned into simple rules of "do it" or "don't do it," losing its earlier variety of meanings. These shifts also affected performers. Applause stopped feeling like a real conversation with the audience. In opera especially, singers began to see it as just part of the usual deal with the crowd.
By the 19th century, applause had become standard and expected.
It was no longer a special reward like before, but something everyone assumed would happen.

G. In the 21st century we're reinventing applause, to make it what it used to be: a coded form of communication. Our kind of applause matters more now, in many ways, because it is no longer momentary and short-lived, but is far more permanent instead.

question_groups.body:
In the 18th century, people could show their superiority by understanding when either ____ (23) or applause was appropriate.

questions.text: In the 18th century, people could show their superiority by understanding when either ____ (23) or applause was appropriate.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
Vào thế kỷ 18, người ta có thể thể hiện sự tinh tế của mình bằng cách hiểu khi nào thì ____ hoặc vỗ tay là phù hợp.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: Cấu trúc "either ___ or applause" — chỗ trống cần một danh từ song song với applause (tiếng vỗ tay), đối lập về nghĩa.

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
show their superiority ~ a sign of good taste and manners
18th century ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
understanding when... was appropriate ~ knowing when to maintain silence — and when to clap

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Khán giả học được rằng việc biết khi nào nên giữ im lặng — và khi nào nên vỗ tay — là dấu hiệu của sự tinh tế và lịch thiệp" (Audiences learned that knowing when to maintain silence — and when to clap — was a sign of good taste and manners).

Bước 5: Đáp án: silence
quotes: Audiences learned that knowing when to maintain silence—and when to clap—was a sign of good taste and manners.

questions.text: Performers in the 18th century, in particular those singing in the ____ (24), no longer had a meaningful dialogue with their audiences.

Các nghệ sĩ biểu diễn vào thế kỷ 18, đặc biệt là những người hát trong ____, không còn có sự giao tiếp thực sự với khán giả nữa.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: "those singing in the ___" — chỗ trống cần một danh từ chỉ thể loại nghệ thuật biểu diễn có ca hát.

meaningful dialogue ~ a real conversation with the audience

those singing ~ singers

Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Tiếng vỗ tay không còn cảm giác như một cuộc trò chuyện thực sự với khán giả nữa. Đặc biệt trong opera, các ca sĩ bắt đầu coi đó chỉ là một phần trong thỏa thuận thông thường với đám đông" (Applause stopped feeling like a real conversation with the audience. In opera especially, singers began to see it as just part of the usual deal with the crowd).

Bước 5: Đáp án: opera
quotes: In opera especially, singers began to see it as just part of the usual deal with the crowd.

Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
Vào thế kỷ 19, tiếng vỗ tay không còn được trao như một ____ cho các nghệ sĩ biểu diễn nữa.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:

Dấu hiệu: "offered as a ___" — chỗ trống cần một danh từ đếm được (có mạo từ a), chỉ thứ gì đó được trao tặng như một sự ghi nhận đặc biệt.

Bước 5: Đáp án: reward
quotes: It was no longer a special reward like before, but something everyone assumed would happen.

questions.text: Nowadays our expressions of approval are seen as ____ (26) in comparison to the applause of the past.
